belay.14: At the foot of the Great Gendarme, where a bolted rappel anchor sits.
belay.15: On a comfortable perch on top of the pillar, once the first 5.9 Gendarme pitch is done.

belay.1: At a bolted station just below the Lithuanian Lip roof.
belay.8: On a small seat built from a couple of pitons and a cam or two.
belay.9: On a sheltered, tree-dotted triangular ledge, anchored in a finger crack.
belay.10: At a large tree, or alternatively off nearby crack placements.
belay.12: At a bolted anchor in an alcove near the summit shoulder, where the descent gully starts.

belay.1: On a ledge near a patch of yellow lichen and a pine tree.
belay.3: On a long ledge with a big horn, at a two-bolt anchor.
belay.5: Just to the right of the Block Ceiling.
belay.9: At the highest point of M&M Ledge, up and left of the previous stance.
belay.10: On a small terrace beneath an obvious splitter wide hand crack.
belay.11: At the bolted anchor on the clean slab beneath the Hercan Roofs.

belay.P1: At a good belay at the left end of the ledge reached at the top of the slabs.
belay.P2: At an anchor in the next major crack or gully, up and right.
belay.P3: On an indistinct ledge at the top of the friable corners, with a fixed knifeblade in place.
belay.P4: At a stance beside some flakes at the end of the rising rightward traverse.
belay.P5: At an uncomfortable stance in the right-hand crack past the roof, on a good #3 cam.
belay.P6: On a heathery ledge beside the big gully, reached up the rib alongside it.
belay.P8: At an anchor below the steeper wall, just above the saddle on the ridge crest.

belay.4: A big sloping ledge reached after moving left across the water streak.
belay.6: A ledge on the left with a two-bolt anchor, the best stance on the route and good for cutting rope drag.
belay.1-2: A two-bolt anchor on the right side of the buttress, at the foot of a short chimney.

belay.4: Past the large ledge with a dead snag: traverse left above it and go around the corner above a live tree to the stance.
belay.5: On the large ledge system at the top of the featured vertical face.
belay.8: Just above the large roof, at the first anchor; the higher belay is uncomfortable.
belay.9: A small stance reached by exiting left at the top of the overhanging face; skip the mid-face anchor, where a bolt spins.

belay.2: At a small stance out right, after climbing behind and over the big chockstone.
belay.4: At the left-hand end of the traverse that follows the quartz dike.
belay.6: At a tree growing on a ledge.
belay.7: On nuts at the foot of the steep headwall.
